probable_cause: Lambda function quote-processor-prod has hit its concurrency limit with 450 throttles in 1 minute during peak quote submission window (2-4pm EST), likely due to reserved concurrency set too low or a slow downstream dependency (RDS/DynamoDB) holding connections longer than expected.
immediate_actions: 1. CHECK SQS QUEUE DEPTH NOW: Run 'aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics --namespace AWS/SQS --metric-name ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible' for the quote-processor queue — if depth exceeds 100K, escalate to P1 immediately.

2. CHECK RESERVED CONCURRENCY: Run 'aws lambda get-function-concurrency --function-name quote-processor-prod' — if set below 500, temporarily increase to 1000 via 'aws lambda put-function-concurrency --function-name quote-processor-prod --reserved-concurrent-executions 1000' after confirming account-level limit has headroom.

3. CHECK RDS CONNECTION POOL: Query CloudWatch for DatabaseConnections metric on the RDS instance — if connections are near max, Lambda is holding connections due to slow queries or timeout misconfiguration; check for long-running queries via RDS Performance Insights immediately.
healthcare_impact: Insurance quote requests are actively failing for end users attempting to obtain coverage pricing during peak afternoon submission window; patients and brokers cannot receive quotes, delaying insurance enrollment decisions and potentially impacting coverage start dates.
escalate_if: SQS queue depth exceeds 100K messages, throttle count increases above 1000 in any 5-minute window, RDS connections are maxed out, or throttling continues beyond 15 minutes without improvement after concurrency increase.
